previous.changeLog: Maintenance release — internal cleanup and stability improvements. Updating is recommended.

current.changeLog:
Settings toggles — a new in-game settings panel (via ModsSettingsAPI) lets you enable or
disable the Garage widget and the in-battle widget independently.
Resolution-robust garage widget — the hangar percentile bar now anchors reliably and matches
the tank-card box height across screen resolutions and interface scales.
Native-styled tooltip — the garage MoE award tooltip now reuses World of Tanks' own tooltip
look.
In-battle overlay tweak — small horizontal position adjustment to the live in-battle overlay.
Bundles the ModsSettingsAPI dependency (added automatically by the installer if missing).

previous.changeLog: Richer buff tooltips. Field-modification and skill-tree buff lines now render like the game's own perk tooltip: the parameter icon, the change value colored green for a buff / red for a nerf (orange in color-blind mode), and the stat it affects — e.g. +50 HP to vehicle hit points, -0.10 s to aiming time. Absolute values now show their unit; the buff/nerf color follows the game's own classification, so a beneficial reduction still reads as green. Fix: sub-unit buff numbers are no longer dropped from upgrade tooltips. A small add KPI on a dispersion-scale hundredth (e.g. gun dispersion -0.01) used to lose its figure, so the tooltip showed only the qualitative sentence with no magnitude. The number now survives while a genuine ~zero still collapses.

current.changeLog:
Switch bar modes from the title. A vehicle often qualifies for several bar modes at once (research / field modifications, elite system / elite rewards). The next available mode's title now shows dimmed beside the current heading — hover to brighten it, click to swap the bar to that mode. With two modes it toggles A↔B; with three or more it cycles forward. Your choice is remembered per vehicle across restarts.
Localized settings panel. The ModsSettingsAPI settings panel now follows the client's language. Bar stays put on resolution / UI-scale changes. Switching resolution or UI scale (e.g. 4K→1080p) live no longer leaves the bar shifted — auto positions re-derive and pinned positions rescale proportionally, and the settings panel shows the correct default for the new viewport.
